source_analysis.skill: Find original pivot-column indices by reducing a general matrix to row echelon form and identifying each nonzero row’s leading entry.
reasoning_steps: Convert the given matrix to REF by row swaps and/or row replacement.
Identify the first nonzero entry in each nonzero REF row.
Map their column indices back to the original matrix and select the complete subset.
invariants: Column ordering matters; row ordering can change without changing the answer.
Select original columns, not transformed column vectors.
Within moderate difficulty preserve sparse matrices and comparable one-swap workload.
permitted_variations: Vary nonzero integers and signs while preserving suitable workload.
Vary eligible pivot-column subsets by constructing sparse row-equivalent REF matrices, including leading zero columns, internal nonpivot columns, and terminal nonpivot columns.
Change row permutation, matrix label, and checkbox order; derive column vectors and solutions consistently.
Within justified shapes vary rank where comparable workload permits; do not freeze every answer-bearing role merely because an example has it.
